questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are not safe to use.
Can be used on rear tires.
Can be used when carrying heavy loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded should never be used.

questions.question: Having anti-lock brakes on only one axle:

options.text: Will not help with braking.
Will give you better control when braking.
Will likely break the air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will give you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle has anti-lock brakes on one axle, the driver has more control while braking than without any anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Get upset.
Accept it and drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive safely.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation while driving safely.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It distracts your mind and your hands.
A message might upset you.
People get too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts your mind and your hands.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention off the road and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop soon to:

options.text: Check if the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.
Fill the tire with air.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance away to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, you should:

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.
Back toward the driver's side.
Back toward the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back toward the driver's side.
questions.explanation: If you need to back your trailer but cannot go straight, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: It has rained recently.
The nuts may be loose.
The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts may be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:

options.text: Keep pumping the brakes.
Turn the vehicle off.
Drive into an open field.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive into an open field.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail while driving downhill, first look for an escape ramp. If there is no ramp, find another place to stop, such as an open field or a road that goes uphill.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, follow it by:

options.text: Not changing anything. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turning the steering wheel harder in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel opposite to the direction you want the trailer to turn. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow it.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should apply the brakes:

options.text: The same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
While putting the vehicle in neutral.
Using only the hand brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One system for the left side of the truck and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the rear axle brakes. The other controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When you drive too slowly.
When you are stopped.
When you take a turn too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you take a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To avoid rolling over, drive slowly on ramps and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when pulling trailers.

questions.question: Before a pre-trip inspection, why should you look under the vehicle?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on an incline.
To check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
To see if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: When approaching your vehicle, check its general condition. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?

options.text: Use water.
Stay inside the vehicle.
Wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them put out the fire.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and confront the driver.
Stop a safe distance away, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a safe distance away, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and tell them about the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: When should you start a left turn?

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
At or after reaching the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after reaching the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start your left turn only when you reach the center of the intersection. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle could hit another vehicle because of off-tracking.

questions.question: At what air pressure will an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: Between 20 and 45 psi.
Between 75 and 105 psi.
Between 50 and 65 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve will pop out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that operates the trailer brakes.
A valve that shows the fuel level.
A valve that limits the amount of cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that operates the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve, also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar, operates the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while the vehicle is moving could cause a skid.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
It will be faster.
It is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps and makes it less likely you will forget to check something.

questions.question: How should you press the brake pedal when stopping?

options.text: Press down quickly with both feet.
Press down gradually.
Lift up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually. This helps the vehicle stop smoothly and safely.
